title: Peace Delivered, Pass It On:
title_short: Peace Delivered · Carousel · Pass It On
format: 4:5 carousel · 1080×1350 stills (the brief asks for a 4:5 Instagram carousel)
headline: The chain is the story: a kid named Olive drew a card, it went to a stranger on the train, and now he has someone else's message to pass on.
story: This carousel is about the hand-off, repeated, not one delivery. Olive's drawing becomes a postcard, Kalindi gives it to a man on the B train, tells him the back story and asks him to pass his own message on.
The seven slides are built (2 Sept, from the RAW MXF). This page is the plan for the final set: the same slides with the fixes in each row, then the call to action with the SFCG logo.
do: Keep the chain in order: the drawing, kids color peace, Olive's card, passed on, the ask, now you have theirs.
Every quote word for word from 764_3845.
Keep the card or the train in every slide, so the journey reads.
SFCG horizontal logo and sfcg.org on the last slide only.
dont: Never Olive's face, or any child's face: hands and the drawing only, until Kalindi confirms a release.
No Preemptive Love branding. Never SFCG or CGLA as a label (sfcg.org as the web address is fine).
Do not change her words to make them read better.
Do not open on a close-up with no setup.

decisions.b: The Peace Delivered push ran 1 to 21 Sept. These slides were built on 2 Sept and never went to SFCG. Atdhe decides: send them to Kalindi now as an evergreen Peace Delivered post, or close the item.

decisions.t: One look for all three carousels
decisions.b: This set uses the older look (blue #1E6FD6 pills, serif italic). The ten 3-slide Peace Delivered sets use the SFCG Brand Refresh 2024 look with the logo band. Atdhe picks one look for all.
Atdhe signs off the call-to-action wording against SFCG's monthly-donor ask. Kalindi confirms Olive's release before any child's face is used (none is used now).

client_note: Why this matters: the campaign's whole idea is deliver, then pass it on. This carousel shows the chain, so a viewer sees how one small card travels.
